content: The provided text is a detailed list of drug interactions involving sulfamethoxazole and various other medications. 1. Sulfamethoxazole interacts with oral forms of hormones, such as conjugated estrogens, estradiol, and ethinyl estradiol, by altering intestinal flora. This may reduce the effectiveness of these hormones, but the risk of contraceptive failure is low. Caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Sulfamethoxazole decreases the effectiveness of the BCG live vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Administration of live bacterial vaccines should be delayed until antibiotic therapy is completed. 3. Sulfamethoxazole increases the effects of bemiparin, bivalirudin, dalteparin, enoxaparin, fondaparinux, and heparin by decreasing their metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. These interactions are serious, and alternative drugs should be considered. 4. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels of bosentan, carvedilol, celecoxib, diclofenac, diltiazem, dronabinol, eltrombopag, ethotoin, etravirine, flurbiprofen, fluvastatin, and ibuprofen by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Monitoring and caution are recommended. 5. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels of glimepiride, glipizide, and glyburide by plasma protein binding competition. Caution and monitoring are necessary, as strong CYP2C9 inhibitors may further decrease glyburide metabolism. 6. Sulfamethoxazole increases the toxicity of dapsone (both systemic and topical) by decreasing its metabolism. Co-administration increases systemic exposure to dapsone and its metabolites, potentially inducing methemoglobinemia. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 7. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels of digoxin by altering intestinal flora and through competition for renal tubular clearance. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 8. Sulfamethoxazole interacts with drugs that prolong the QTc interval, such as chlorpromazine, clarithromycin, clomipramine, desipramine, disopyramide, dolasetron, dofetilide, droperidol, erythromycin (various forms), flecainide, fluconazole, fluvoxamine, haloperidol, and formoterol. These combinations may increase the risk of QTc prolongation, necessitating therapy modification and close monitoring. 9. Sulfamethoxazole decreases the levels of biotin, folic acid, and dosulepin by altering intestinal flora or inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. These interactions are minor, but their clinical significance is unknown. 10. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels of furosemide, hydrochlorothiazide, and other thiazide diuretics (e.g., bendroflumethiazide, chlorothiazide, chlorthalidone, cyclopenthiazide) through unspecified mechanisms. These interactions may increase the risk of hyponatremia. Monitoring is recommended. 11. Sulfamethoxazole increases the toxicity of ganciclovir through pharmacodynamic synergy. Monitoring is advised, as the clinical significance is unknown. 12. Sulfamethoxazole decreases the levels of clomipramine, desipramine, and doxepin through unspecified mechanisms. These interactions are minor, but their clinical significance is unknown. 13. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels of fosphenytoin by decreasing its metabolism. Monitoring is recommended, as the clinical significance is unknown. 14. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels of eluxadoline by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Due to incomplete information on eluxadoline metabolism, caution is advised when co-administering with strong CYP2C9/10 inhibitors. 15. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels of erythromycin (various forms) and fluoxetine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Monitoring and caution are recommended. 16. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels of felbamate by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Monitoring is advised, as the clinical significance is unknown. 17. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels of glucarpidase substrates (e.g., leucovorin, reduced folates, and folate antimetabolites) by increasing metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 18. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels of ibuprofen by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended, as the clinical significance is unknown. 19. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels of fluphenazine and fluvastatin by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Monitoring and caution are advised. 20. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels of epinephrine and racemic epinephrine, both of which prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 21. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels of erdafitinib by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. If co-administration with strong CYP2C9 inhibitors cannot be avoided, close monitoring for adverse reactions is necessary, and dose adjustments should be considered. 22. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels of erythromycin base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, and stearate, all of which prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 23. Sulfamethoxazole decreases the levels of estropipate by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 24. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels of ethacrynic acid by an unspecified mechanism. Monitoring is recommended, as the clinical significance is unknown. 25. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels of etravirine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended, as the clinical significance is unknown. 26. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels of fondaparinux by decreasing its metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be considered. 27. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels of glimepiride, glipizide, and glyburide by plasma protein binding competition. Caution and monitoring are necessary, as strong CYP2C9 inhibitors may further decrease glyburide metabolism. 28. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels of haloperidol, which prolongs the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 29. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels of hydralazine by an unspecified mechanism. Monitoring is recommended, as the clinical significance is unknown. 30. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels of ibuprofen by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended, as the clinical significance is unknown. This list provides a comprehensive overview of the interactions between sulfamethoxazole and other drugs, emphasizing the need for caution, monitoring, and in some cases, the use of alternative therapies.
